evidence: Frozen task/task.toml [environment] section (lines 20-24) contains only build_timeout_sec = 600.0, network_mode = "public", cpus = 2, memory_mb = 4096; no docker_image key. Recursive grep for 'docker_image' over the frozen task and template returns nothing (rc=1), and grep -i 'image' over task.toml returns nothing, so no prebuilt image is declared under [environment], [verifier.environment] or elsewhere. The agent Dockerfile (task/environment/Dockerfile:1-26) has active build steps that matter to the task: FROM node:22-bookworm-slim, apt install of sqlite3/git, pinned global npm install of express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1, COPY instructions/ /instructions/ and COPY assets/ /assets/ (the brief's referenced files), and /app git init. Because docker_image is absent, Harbor builds this Dockerfile, so these steps are live, not dead code. Hashes: task.toml ac664d0e...8f26, environment/Dockerfile 0a75419e...67d1, tests/Dockerfile 72998ab8...5fdd computed on the frozen bytes match manifest.json lines 10, 26, 29; the agent Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (same hash, manifest line 56; diff empty). The task.toml [environment]/[verifier.environment] blocks equal the template's (template differs only in CHANGE_ME identity fields). Adversarial check: the failure mode this row targets would be e.g. docker_image = "node:22-bookworm-slim" added under [environment]; the agent would then start without /instructions, /assets, express/better-sqlite3, and an initialized /app repo, while the Dockerfile silently looks correct. No such key exists, so that counterexample does not apply. Conversely, no conforming alternative is penalized: the row is a static config property independent of the submitted app. This is a static source check; I did not build the image (Docker build success belongs to row 15 / runtime evidence, not to this row).
